content:
Messaging platform Telegram is sending out alerts to users running outdated versions of iOS, urging them to install the latest available software update. Here are the details.

Telegram tells iPhone users to update iOS

Over the past few months, Apple has released multiple iOS updates to address security vulnerabilities, amid the growing use of AI tools to discover security flaws and develop exploits.

Throughout this year, Apple has also stepped up the frequency of its iOS security releases across multiple generations of the operating system.

Based on the company’s security releases page, Apple has issued iOS updates with published security advisories on 13 separate dates so far this year, up from 12 during the same period in 2025 and nine in 2024.

The number of vulnerabilities addressed in those updates has also increased considerably. Apple’s iOS security advisories list fixes for 707 distinct vulnerabilities affecting the iPhone so far this year, more than double the 334 Apple addressed in all of 2025. In 2024, that figure was 302.

In other words, Apple has addressed more iOS vulnerabilities so far this year than in 2024 and 2025 combined.

Granted, Apple is now issuing security updates for more generations of iOS than it was last year, but the company itself confirmed back in June that it was accelerating the rollout of security fixes in response to the growing capabilities of AI-powered hacking tools.

Additionally, Apple has issued at least two waves of mercenary spyware threat notifications over the past few months, reaching targeted users in 110 countries in August and 99 countries in late October.

Now, Telegram is issuing security warnings of its own.

In a post on X yesterday, Telegram founder and CEO Pavel Durov claimed that “iPhone users are being hacked on a massive scale,” noting that “just opening a website can be enough to get you hacked.”

For this reason, he said, Telegram has been sending out a security alert to all of its users running older versions of iOS, urging them to update their iPhones.

Durov didn’t elaborate on the nature or extent of the alleged attacks, nor did he specify which iOS vulnerabilities were being exploited. That said, Apple addressed more than 30 WebKit vulnerabilities with the release of iOS 27.2 in late October alone, some of which could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code through maliciously crafted web content.

To be clear, Apple did not indicate that any of those vulnerabilities had been actively exploited.

As of this writing, the latest available versions of iOS for actively supported iPhones are iOS 27.2.1, iOS 26.7.3, and iOS 18.7.12, depending on which iOS generation your device is compatible with or currently running.
